chunks: Al-Kulayni, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the world in six days, then He deducted it from the days of the year, so the year is three hundred and fifty-four days.
Sha'ban is never complete, and by Allah, the month of Ramadan is never deficient.
And the obligation (of fasting) will never be deficient.
And to complete the number.
Shawwal is twenty-nine days, and Dhu al-Qi'dah is thirty days.
And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten.
Dhu al-Hijjah is twenty-nine days, and Muharram is thirty days.
Then the months after that are one complete month and one deficient month.

And this report is similar to what preceded regarding the validity of using it as evidence, like what we previously stated: that it is a single report which does not necessitate knowledge or action, and it is not objected to with its like against the apparent meaning of the Quran and mutawatir reports, and that although the words and meanings differ, the report is one and the chain is one.
And also, this report contains explanation that reveals it was not established from an infallible Imam (peace be upon him).
From that is that the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, 'And We appointed for Moses thirty nights,' does not necessitate the continuation of such a month to be complete in Dhu al-Qi'dah.

And the agreement of the completeness of Dhu al-Qi'dah in the days of Moses (peace be upon him) does not necessitate its completeness in future times, nor does it indicate that it remained thus in the past.

And if the matter is as we mentioned, the attribution of the explanation for the completeness of Dhu al-Qi'dah forever based on what the Quran included of its completeness at one time to the Truth from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is invalidated.
Especially since it is also an explanation for the completeness of the month of Ramadan.
And there is no specific relationship between them regarding completeness.
And the deduction of six days from the year does not prevent the deficiency in two or three months in succession and the completeness of three or four consecutive months.
So how can the explanation be valid with a meaning that reason, custom, and language do not necessitate?
And similarly, the explanation for the month of Ramadan being thirty days forever, based on the obligations not being deficient.
Because the deficiency of the month from thirty days does not necessitate deficiency in the obligatory act within it.
And it is established that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not obligate us with the act of the days themselves, and it is valid that we are not obligated with the act of time.
Rather, He obligated us with the action within the days and the act within the time.
So the deficiency of time relative to another is not a deficiency in the action by attribution.

Do you not see that whoever had an obligation in a specific month, and he fulfilled it in that month as defined for him, starting from its beginning and ending it at its end, that he has completed what was obligatory upon him, even if the month was deficient from completeness?

And Muslims agree that the woman observing the waiting period by months, if her husband divorces her at the beginning of a month, and she completes three months in it, one being complete (thirty days) and two of them each being twenty-nine days, that she has fulfilled the obligation of Allah upon her regarding the waiting period in its completeness without deficiency.
And the deficiency of the two months does not extend to the obligation upon the woman regarding the waiting period, as we mentioned.

And if a person vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to fast a month following his arrival from travel or recovery from illness, and it happened that the month following that was twenty-nine days, and he fasted it from its beginning to its end, he would have fulfilled the obligation of Allah in it in its completeness.
And the deficiency of the month would not result in deficiency of the obligation he fulfilled in it.

And the objection also regarding the month of Ramadan not being except thirty days, based on His saying, 'And to complete the number,' is invalidated in its establishment from an infallible Imam by what we mentioned regarding the completeness of the obligation fulfilled in what is deficient from the month of thirty days.
Despite the apparent meaning of the Quran indicating that the command to complete the number is directed to the meaning of making up for what was missed of fasting.

So whoever among you sees the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period.

So He informed that He obligated the traveler and the sick, upon their breaking fast in the month, to make up for it in other days, so that they complete thereby the number of what was missed from them of fasting the month that passed.
And in that is no specification of what the making up falls upon.
Rather, it is a command regarding what is obligatory of making up the missed, whatever it may be.

And this phrase that we mentioned indicates that the mentioned explanation for the completeness of the month of Ramadan being thirty days is fabricated and not valid from the Imams (peace be upon them).
And if this hadith were safe from all that we mentioned, what its wording included would not be contradictory to the practice regarding the crescents.
Nor would it necessitate ruling for the validity of its opposite.

And that is that the denial of the general public regarding what they claimed of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasting the month of Ramadan twenty-nine days more than fasting it thirty days does not prevent that he fasted it twenty-nine days.
Except that his fasting it thus was less than his fasting it thirty days.

And if his fasting it during the period of its obligation upon him in his life necessitated thirty days, it would not prevent the change of the situation in that and its being twenty-nine days in some times after him, as we prefaced in the statement regarding that.
And the saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast except a complete month does not indicate that the month of fasting is thirty days in all cases.
Because fasting is not the month, and it is the act of the faster, and the month is the movements of the sphere, and they are the act of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And the description of completeness is for the fasting which is the act of the servant, not the description of the time which is the act of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And we have clarified that in what preceded.
And using His saying, 'And to complete the number,' as evidence for that does not necessitate what the people of numbers thought, that the month of fasting will not be twenty-nine days.

Because completing the number of the deficient month by acting in all of it is like completing the number of the complete month by acting in all of it, and no one of the rational ones differs in that.
And the saying that Shawwal is twenty-nine days does not indicate what they said.
Rather, the report allows for it being thus sometimes, without it being thus necessarily in all cases.
And the saying that Dhu al-Qi'dah is thirty days and does not decrease forever, its basis is what we mentioned, that it is not deficient forever, so it is not incomplete at one time.
And the objection for that by His saying, 'And We appointed for Moses thirty nights,' confirms this interpretation.
Because it indicated its occurrence in a time from the times, which the Quran mentioned as thirty days.
So it necessitated that it is not deficient forever, but it may be complete, even if deficiency is permissible upon it.
And that which indicates what we mentioned regarding the permissibility of deficiency upon Dhu al-Qi'dah in some times is what was narrated.
ai.seo_question: Is the month of Ramadan always thirty days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kulayni’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* presents a specific view that Ramadan is perpetually thirty days and Sha'ban never completes, linking this to the Quranic command to 'complete the number.' However, the accompanying scholarly critique argues this reasoning is weak, as the verse primarily mandates making up missed fasts rather than fixing the lunar month's duration, thereby supporting the established Shia practice of variable month lengths (29 or 30 days).
